title: John Abraham Bets on European Cricket — and Joins Jonty Rhodes and Faf du Plessis at the Rotterdam Dockers
excerpt: The Bollywood actor becomes co-owner of a Rotterdam franchise in the inaugural European T20 Premier League, cricket's first ICC-backed multi-nation league in Europe
body:
Bollywood and cricket have never been far apart. Shah Rukh Khan has Kolkata Knight Riders. Preity Zinta has Punjab Kings. And now John Abraham has the Rotterdam Dockers.

The actor and sports entrepreneur has joined the ownership group of the Netherlands-based franchise ahead of the inaugural season of the European T20 Premier League (ETPL), a new ICC-sanctioned tournament that will run from August 26 to September 20 across venues in Ireland, Scotland, and the Netherlands.

Abraham joins a strikingly cricket-heavy ownership consortium that includes three South African greats — Jonty Rhodes, Faf du Plessis, and Heinrich Klaasen — alongside Managing Partner Madhukar Shree. The ETPL itself was co-founded by Abhishek Bachchan, adding yet another Bollywood connection to the project.

"Cricket has the power to inspire, unite and create opportunities, and that's exactly what excites me about the European T20 Premier League," Abraham said. "Europe represents one of cricket's most exciting growth markets, and Rotterdam Dockers has the vision, leadership and ambition to build something truly special."

## What is the ETPL?



> **""John brings tremendous passion, energy and a proven track record of building successful sporting ventures," said Madhukar Shree, Managing Partner of the Rotterdam franchise."**


The European T20 Premier League is being billed as the first franchise-based T20 league to span multiple countries in Europe. It is jointly backed by Cricket Ireland, Cricket Scotland, and the Royal Dutch Cricket Association (KNCB), with six franchises representing cities across all three nations: the Rotterdam Dockers, Amsterdam Flames, Dublin Guardians, Glasgow Cosmic, Edinburgh Castle Rockers, and a Belfast franchise.

The 32-match inaugural season will feature a format similar to other successful franchise leagues, with a player draft system. Each team will carry eight home-nation players and one development player from a European country outside the three host nations, ensuring a deliberate focus on growing local talent alongside established international stars.

Player draft registration opened in June 2026, with eligible cricketers from Ireland, Scotland, and the Netherlands invited to submit their names through the official ETPL website.

## Bollywood's deepening footprint in franchise cricket

Abraham's investment is not his first venture into sports ownership. The actor has long been associated with football through his involvement in the Indian Super League, where he owned the NorthEast United FC franchise. His move into cricket follows a broader pattern of Indian entertainment figures treating franchise ownership as both a commercial play and a brand extension.

What makes the ETPL investment distinctive is the geography. Unlike the IPL, the Caribbean Premier League, or the SA20 — established leagues where Indian entertainment money has flowed before — European cricket is genuinely uncharted territory. The Netherlands, Ireland, and Scotland are all Associate nations that have produced talented international cricketers like Paul Stirling, Ryan ten Doeschate, and Richie Berrington, but have long struggled for the funding and visibility that a franchise league can bring.

A tournament backed by a robust ICC sanction and high-profile investors could shift the equation. And for Abraham, the brand visibility across Europe — a continent where cricket is still trying to find its footing — represents an opportunity that the more crowded league markets do not.

## The diaspora dimension

For Indian cricket fans living in Europe, the ETPL fills a gap. It offers live, high-quality franchise cricket played in a convenient time zone and, in some cases, in cities with thriving South Asian communities. The Netherlands has a significant Indian and Surinamese-Indian population; Ireland's Indian community has grown substantially over the past decade; and Scotland's South Asian diaspora has been a pillar of grassroots cricket for generations.

"John brings tremendous passion, energy and a proven track record of building successful sporting ventures," said Madhukar Shree, Managing Partner of the Rotterdam franchise. "His involvement strengthens our vision of creating a franchise that not only competes at the highest level but also leaves a lasting impact on the growth of the game."

The ETPL's debut season is still two months away, and questions about commercial viability and long-term sustainability are natural for any new league. But with Bollywood backing, international cricketing pedigree in the ownership group, and an underserved but enthusiastic European market, the Rotterdam Dockers are staking a claim that stretches well beyond the boundary rope.
